title: Concrete Foot Paths (Type 5,6,8)

project_info.label: Location
project_info.value: Curtin University, Brand Drive & Hayman rd, Bentley, Western Australia

standards.heading: Referenced Standards
rows: Guidelines on earthworks for commercial & residential developments

inspection_legend: Type of Inspection H = HOLD W = WITNESS R = REVIEW

activities.activity: Review SOW, SWMS, drawings and associated Specifications.
criteria: Contractual accepted specifications& Approved SWMS
Surface firm, level, and free of soft spots
No standing water or unsuitable material
Subgrade compacted to ≥95% MMDD
Subbase
Subbase material meets project requirements (clean, free of organics, correct grading)
Subbase material achieves minimum CBR 45%
Bedding Course Sand
Bedding sand is clean, coarse, free from organics
Subbase
Placed in uniform layers (≤150 mm compacted thickness)
Compaction ≥ 95% Modified (AS1289.5.2.1)
Subbase material moisture content to be maintained within OMC ±2%
Surface trimmed to tolerance: +10 / −25 mm per civil spec subbase tolerances
No contamination or segregation
Bedding Course Sand
Spread evenly to 50mm ±10 mm thickness
No soft spots, voids, ruts or moisture pockets
Graded smooth and level prior to reinforcement placement
Concrete Mix Requirements:
N25 Concrete Grade (minimum)
SL Cement Type
No breccia type aggregate permitted
20mm Nominal Aggregate Size
Slump ≤100 mm
Concrete must comply with AS 3600 (structural concrete)
No unauthorised water addition on site
Formwork Set to correct RLs, finished surface levels, and crossfalls as shown on drawings
Formwork straight, rigid, braced and free from distortion
Internal faces smooth and clean to ensure uniform finish
Reinforcement clean and free of rust, scale, oil, mud, paint or contaminants
Reinforcement installed to design
Mesh supported on approved chairs/spacers to achieve correct cover
Top cover: 40 mm
Bottom cover: 50 mm
Mesh overlaps per GN0003 reinforcement notes:
Laps to include cross‑wire and meet the minimum lengths per mesh standards (typically 225 mm) unless otherwise shown
Mesh placed centrally in slab depth unless otherwise detailed
Tie wires used where required to maintain spacing and stability
Concrete placed to full depth without segregation or excessive freefall
Vibrators used throughout placement to ensure full compaction
Concrete spread evenly and continuously to avoid cold joints
Slump tested and confirmed ≤ 100 mm maximum and Compressive Strength Cylinders Taken (7 Day & 28 Day)
Concrete screeded to the required cross-section profile, free of depressions or high areas
Surface closed and shaped uniformly
Edges neatly finished along formwork lines
Any transitions or adjoining pavement edges matched to drawings
Expansion Joints Expansion joints at maximum 6.0 m centres 10 mm Abelflex with rip‑off strip adhered to previously cast concrete face
Contraction Joints Maximum spacing = 1.5 × the width of the footpath Joints to match kerb joints and adjacent pavements where possible
Saw Cutting Saw‑cutting using soft‑cut saws to prevent shrinkage cracking Saw Cut Grooves Clean and free of debris
7 Day minimum Curing Period
Concrete cured using approved non-oil-based curing compound, or clear plastic sheet covering slab
Entire surface to be uniformly covered / coated
Footpath finish is uniform, smooth, and true to profile.
Surface is free of defects, including honeycombing, segregation, surface tearing, excessive trowel marks, and edge damage.
No unplanned cracking present.
Footpath width, alignment, and levels comply with design requirements
Crossfall and surface profile meet drawing requirements with no ponding or deformation.
All joints installed in the correct design locations and matching adjacent kerb/pavement joints where applicable.
NCRs Closed (If Applicable)
